description: P-51D Mustang 1/4 scale, 120 cc class (plans/short-kit class: Chad Veich 1/4 plans, Jerry Bates 1/4, FokkeRC 1/4 short kit): 2.820 m span giant-scale P-51D Mustang, 120 cc gasoline. Physics derived by research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py (P51-05, realism pass P51-06/09/12/13) from the full-size airplane scaled 1/4 and documented NACA/RC-class sources; exercised by scripted tests/test_p51_envelope.gd and test_p51_ground.gd. Not flight-identified on a real model. Flaps are simulated; retractable gear is modeled, with airborne starts stowed. Visual geometry lives in assets/aircraft/p51d-mustang-120/geometry.json.

servo_full_throw_time.source: placeholder: one normalized command from neutral to this aircraft's full modeled throw in 0.18 s; actual servo speed, voltage/load, horn geometry and linkage ratio are unknown, so a published no-load rate per 60 deg cannot determine surface rate

aero.source: Derived from the scaled geometry by research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py (Helmbold/DATCOM, tail volume calibrated to the NACA glide neutral point, strip theory, Schrenk/Reynolds spanwise stall, drag build-up); report research/p51/p51-05/derivation.md. Not flight-identified on a real model.

CL_max.source: three equal-area strips: Schrenk loading and NACA TN 1945 66(2)-415 clmax(Re), including extrapolated 3e5 endpoint and 0.05 painted-finish decrement; flaps up; no P-51 model polar

CL_min.source: cambered section: inverted stall earlier than upright

stall_blend_width.source: NACA TN 1945: at Re 0.7-1e6 the 15 % 6-series stall is rounded (cl flat over ~4 deg, mild drop); which part of the span stalls first comes from the strip offsets (aero.surfaces.wing_station_incidence)

sideslip_blend.source: Sideslip range where the linear beta terms (CYb, Clb, Cnb) give way to their sin(beta) form, finite and restoring up to knife edge

conventions.rates: p_hat = p·b/(2V), q_hat = q·c/(2V), r_hat = r·b/(2V)
conventions.elevator: per radian, positive = trailing edge DOWN (dCm/dElev < 0)
conventions.aileron: per radian per surface, positive = trailing edge DOWN; right and left listed separately
conventions.rudder: per radian, positive = trailing edge LEFT (dCn/dRud < 0)
conventions.axes: lift, drag, side force in wind axes; roll, pitch, yaw moments in body axes about the aero reference point

CL0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: cambered wing at +1 deg incidence + tail at zero body alpha, tail flow angle calibrated to the XP-51 trim curves (P51-19)

CLa.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: Helmbold wing x cos2(dihedral) + downwashed tail

CLq.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail volume + DATCOM wing term

CLde.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail slope x elevator effectiveness

CLda_each.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: strip theory over the aileron span

CD0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: component drag build-up at 25 m/s with the gear UP; the gear-down drag area is landing_gear.retraction (P51-11b), see derivation.md

CL_minD.source: cambered laminar section: minimum drag near half the zero-alpha wing lift

CDda_each.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

CDdr.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

CDde.source: OpenFlightSim UltraStick25e (via the Stik data file); second-order control drag

CYdr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin slope x Sv/S x rudder effectiveness (must equal the vertical surface)

Clb.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 5 deg dihedral (strip theory) + wing at CL_ref + low-wing interference + fin

Clp.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: strip theory with taper + stab + fin

Cldr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: rudder side force x fin height above the ARP

Cm0.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: wing Cm_ac from the UIUC NAA 45-100 camber lines using thin-airfoil theory x0.8 correction, plus tail at zero body alpha with its flow angle CALIBRATED to the XP-51 glide trim curves (NACA MR L-566 Fig. 10; P51-19), about the ARP

Cma.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail about the wing-body ac; the CG transfer gives the static margin

Cmq.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: tail damping about the CG (undownwashed tail slope) x1.1 for wing/fuselage

Cmde.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: elevator lift x tail arm from the ARP

Cmda_each.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: aileron lift increment at its thin-airfoil centre, arm from the ARP

Cnb.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: vertical-fin contribution plus the flight-calibrated body term aero.surfaces.body_cn_beta (P51-25); the shared rule requires Cnb = fin + body

Cnr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin + wing profile drag + fuselage (-0.02 estimated)

Cnda_right.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: adverse yaw 2 K CL_ref Clda, K 0.15 (Nelson, AR 5.8, taper 0.48)

Cndr.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: rudder side force x fin arm from the ARP (must equal the vertical surface)

wing_aileron_effectiveness.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: |Clda_right| 2n b / (CLa sum(y)) over the loader's equal-area tapered strips

wing_station_incidence.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: per-strip angle offsets root -> tip, zero mean: linear washout + Schrenk loading + Re-dependent section clmax (NACA TN 1945); see derivation.md 'stall'

wing_section_cm_ac.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: section Cm_ac: thin-airfoil over the UIUC NAA 45-100 root and tip camber lines (research/p51/p51-13/section.json), blended root -> tip and chord-weighted, x 0.8 (theory/measured, NACA TN 1945)

lift_slope.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: Helmbold x eta 0.9 x (1 - deps/dalpha)

incidence.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: (stab incidence - eps0) / (1 - deps/dalpha) with the +2 deg leading-edge-up setting, plus a -2.30 deg local-flow correction CALIBRATED to the XP-51 glide trim curves (NACA MR L-566 Fig. 10, elevator rms 4.10 -> 0.27 deg; P51-19)

downwash_gradient.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: d(eps)/d(alpha) at the tail: elliptic-wing estimate 2 CLa_w / (pi AR), the same value folded into lift_slope, control_effectiveness and incidence

area.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin + rudder side polygon from assets/aircraft/p51d-mustang-120/geometry.json (P51-01: full-size P-51D dimensions scaled to the kit span)

position.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fin ac: quarter chord at the area-centroid height

lift_slope.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: Helmbold (end-plated AR) x DATCOM sidewash/eta

control_effectiveness.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: thin-airfoil tau x 0.8 / sidewash factor

incidence.source: symmetric fin; engine side thrust not modelled

body_cn_beta.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: CALIBRATED (P51-25): destabilizing body yaw about the ARP so the oracle steady sideslip, balanced about the CG, needs 0.55 deg rudder per deg sideslip, the production P-51D value at 200 mph (NACA RM L6J25 Table I, ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20050019329; approximate slopes over +-1 deg, climb power); DATCOM fuselage alone -0.0232. Lumps fuselage, spinner, canopy and propeller in yaw; geometric scaling does not establish it for the RC model

induced_coefficient.source: research/p51/p51-20/ground_effect_vlm.py: least-squares fit of the faded runtime law to the same-CL induced-drag ratio of an image-method Weissinger VLM of this wing (taper, 5 deg dihedral, washout), x = ARP height / span 0.06-1.5, rms 0.010; ratio 0.63 at x 0.12 (wheels) where Raymer's 33x^1.5 gives 0.58. No fuselage; not measured

induced_exponent.source: research/p51/p51-20/ground_effect_vlm.py: least-squares fit of the faded runtime law to the same-CL induced-drag ratio of an image-method Weissinger VLM of this wing (taper, 5 deg dihedral, washout), x = ARP height / span 0.06-1.5, rms 0.010; ratio 0.63 at x 0.12 (wheels) where Raymer's 33x^1.5 gives 0.58. No fuselage; not measured

downwash_coefficient.source: research/p51/p51-20/ground_effect_vlm.py: least-squares fit of the faded runtime law to the VLM's tail downwash ratio per unit wing lift over the stabilizer quarter-chord line (0.26 m above and 1.28 m behind the ARP), rms 0.015; ratio 0.62 at x 0.12, where the Stik's low-tail fit 25x^2 gives 0.27. No fuselage; not measured

downwash_exponent.source: research/p51/p51-20/ground_effect_vlm.py: least-squares fit of the faded runtime law to the VLM's tail downwash ratio per unit wing lift over the stabilizer quarter-chord line (0.26 m above and 1.28 m behind the ARP), rms 0.015; ratio 0.62 at x 0.12, where the Stik's low-tail fit 25x^2 gives 0.27. No fuselage; not measured

CLadot.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 2 eta CLa_h Sh/S l_h/c deps/dalpha

propulsion.description: 120 cc gasoline twin turning a 4-blade 26x12. Shaft balance (rpm from engine torque against propeller torque), blade-element tables calibrated on Mejzlik's 26x12 2- and 3-blade data, down and right thrust, propeller normal force and P-factor, tail slipstream with swirl (research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py, P51-06/P51-12).

engine.name: Desert Aircraft DA-120 (121 cc twin, 2.45 kg with ignition) or DLE-120

peak_power.source: DA-120 11.7 hp, desertaircraft.com/products/da-120 (2026-10-06): the maker's rating; the installed curve below is lower

peak_power_rpm.source: DA-120 top of the 1300-6900 rpm range (desertaircraft.com)

max_rpm_static.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: full-throttle shaft balance at rest (shaft model)

idle_rpm.source: static idle: DA-120 range starts at 1300 rpm (desertaircraft.com); set a little above for a large propeller

lag_time_constant.source: D5 lag model, unused while the shaft model is present (kept for the format)

power_curve.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: installed full-throttle brake power: generic two-stroke torque shape (estimated; no DA-120 dyno curve published) scaled to a secondary reported anchor, a 28x10 at 6550 rpm static; no retained instrumented test record (Mejzlik 28x10 Cp 0.0238 -> 6901 W)

friction_torque.source: friction and pumping ~12 % of the brake torque at 6900 rpm (YASim 8 %; research synthesis 10-15 %)

idle_power.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: closed-throttle admitted power: holds 1400 rpm static

peak_indicated_power.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: brake + friction power at the curve's peak: the open throttle never limits

propeller.name: 4-blade 26x12 (scale look; heavy for a 120 cc: Biela rates its 26x12 4-blade for 150-160 cc, the DA-120 list gives 3-blade 26x12 / 27x12)

ct_table.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: blade-element/momentum (research/p51/p51-06/bem.py), pitch x1.441 and chord x0.581 fitted to Mejzlik 26x12 2B/3B tables (rms 6.5 %); tabulated into the windmilling branch

cp_table.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: same calibrated blade-element model; Cp < 0 = windmilling

rotating_inertia.source: 4 x Mejzlik's mean per-blade inertia (26x12 2B/3B datasheets) + spinner shell + crank and flywheel 0.002

thrust_line_offset.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: propeller disc centre (thrust line) relative to the inventory CG; [x_aft, y_right, z_up]

thrust_angles.source: down 1.75 deg (Top Flite Giant P-51D manual), right 1 deg (Ziroli 98 in plans); no published full-size or 1/4-scale value

normal_force.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: McCormick blade-element normal force per rad of disc angle of attack (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938), x rho n2 D4; solidity 0.112

pfactor_moment.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: McCormick P-factor yawing moment per rad of disc angle of attack (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938), x rho n2 D5

hub.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: propeller disc centre on the thrust line (le frame)

wash_factor.source: velocity added at the tail per disc induced velocity w (Selig, AIAA 2010-7938, eqs. 17-19, m = V/(V + w)): 0.8 at m = 0 and 1.8 at m >= 0.75, read off the plot of Fig. 5 (approximate); the text gives ~1 at static thrust (free-jet theory) and 'approaches but does not reach 2' (ideal) away from it because of the fuselage

swirl_factor.source: part of the propeller's angular momentum that reaches the tail (wing and fuselage straighten the rest): research synthesis 0.5-0.8; Selig: the swirl offsets ~40 % of the torque roll

vertical_drift.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 1 - d(eps)/d(alpha): the wake drifts with the downwashed flow

propeller_sidewash.source: Ribner, NACA ARR L4I12a (1944) eq. 8: far-wake crossflow of a propeller at incidence, h(a)*v_c + g(a)*N/(2*mdot), applied as published (1); also selects the piecewise swirl quadrature of the legacy pieces (P51-26: the single-centroid swirl was off by up to x2.15 against 1024-strip integration)

bsfc.source: FUEL-08: 500 g/kWh proxy within the documented 406-580 g/kWh small gasoline-engine evidence band (FUEL-00; Moulton 2007 and Horn 2015); not measured on the DA-120

idle_flow.source: FUEL-08: explicit 4.8 g/min idle baseline; no published DA-120/gasoline idle flow found in FUEL-00

landing_gear.description: P51-11b: retractable taildragger: two main wheels and a steerable tail wheel (E1 spring-dampers, E2 tyre friction, E3 field surfaces) on the shared retractable-point-gear-v1 law. Pneumatic RC retracts with sequenced air-cylinder doors (CARF 1:4.3 manual); kinematics, timing and drag are estimates, not measured on a built model.

position.source: wheel bottom from geometry.json (axle station and height measured on the AN 01-60-3 three-view, track 142 in full size per NACA, wheel 6.75 in)

stiffness.source: E1 rule: heave ω·dt 0.09 at 240 Hz (Σk = 10031 N/m for 21.50 kg), split by the static load (11.7 % on the tail wheel) so all three wheels sag alike (21 mm); softer than a real oleo, which a 240 Hz explicit tick cannot resolve

damping.source: damping ratio 0.3 of the loader's m/3 share: sprung oleo legs and tyres, little hydraulic damping in RC retract struts

max_compression.source: breaking travel: a level touchdown at about 2.5 m/s sink reaches it (½mv² against the springs with the static sag); RC practice, not measured

retraction_path.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 129 uniform extension samples of the wheel-bottom point: the geometry.json gear.retraction kinematics (inclined main trunnion axis, forward tail swing) with sequenced doors (door_phase 0.2); the builder animates the same numbers

max_steering.source: AS-02 compatibility default: explicit zero preserves the v1 omitted-steering behavior for this contact

max_compression.source: GP-06c reserve-energy travel: the peak tail compression of a three-point free drop at the former 14 CFR 23.727 reserve velocity, 1.2 x 7 ft/s = 2.56 m/s with wing lift 2/3 W through the CG (23.473(d)/(e)), x1.05 rounded up to 5 mm (research/ground-physics/gp06/reserve_drop.gd: 96 mm). Replaces the estimated 0.08 m, which collapsed in the 7 ft/s limit drop. A full-size certification convention borrowed for RC; not measured strut travel or strength

max_steering.source: steerable tail wheel linked to the rudder, +-25 deg typical for giant-scale retract tail wheels; negative: the tail wheel turns against the rudder trailing edge

retraction_path.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 129 uniform extension samples of the wheel-bottom point: the geometry.json gear.retraction kinematics (inclined main trunnion axis, forward tail swing) with sequenced doors (door_phase 0.2); the builder animates the same numbers

rolling_resistance.source: between a full-size tyre on concrete (JSBSim c172x 0.022) and the Stik's 76 mm wheel (0.04): the 171 mm wheels deform less; per-surface factors (grass) come from the field

breakaway_factor.source: P51-21, as the Stik and Timber (E3b1): static / rolling resistance of a wheel at rest (bearing and axle friction, tyre flat spot, the small mound in front of a wheel parked on grass); the ground knowledge base (docs/research/roadmap-investigations/04, section 3) brackets it at 1.0-1.5 without a measurement and 1.25 is the middle. A luggage-scale pull on a built model (breakaway force, then the steady rolling force) would measure it

side_friction.source: JSBSim c172x static_friction 0.8 (as the Stik, E2)

peak_slip_angle.source: JSBSim FGLGear default Pacejka initial slope (as the Stik, E2)

extension_time.source: pneumatic RC retracts with a sequencer valve (CARF manual: Ultra Precision UP-2/UP-4): doors, about 2 s of leg travel, doors; the full-size gear took 10-15 s

drag_area.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: the gear-down item of the drag build-up (wheels, struts, doors 0.020 m2) x1.1 excrescences, removed from CD0

drag_center.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: deployed wheel-bottom points weighted 0.45/0.45/0.10 (main legs and wheels dominate the frontal area); an estimated drag moment arm

max_angle_deg.source: landing setting, CARF P-51 1:4.3 manual p. 28 (source.json kit.flaps_deg); full-size P-51 50 deg (NACA MR L-566)

takeoff_angle_deg.source: take-off setting, CARF manual p. 28; full-size XP-51 20 deg (NACA MR L-566 Table III)

inner_span_m.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: flap inner end from the centreline: full-size 0.5 m x 1/4 (source.json full_size.flap)

outer_span_m.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: flap outer end from the centreline: full-size 3.2 m x 1/4; XP-51 flap 32.22 sq ft, chord 23/17 in (NACA MR L-566) agrees

hinge_fraction.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 1 - flap chord fraction 0.21 (scaled full-size flap)

extension_time.source: slowed RC flap servo (typical 2-4 s radio setting); the full-size flap took about 15 s

max_speed_mps.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: advisory: full-size 165 mph IAS full-flap placard (secondary sources) at equal CL 0.555, landing weight 9,000 lb; not a simulation clamp

elevator_mix_per_flap_fraction.source: no radio mix: the CARF manual (flap-angle source) specifies none; Hangar 9's 7 %/14 % up mix belongs to a different airframe. The flap pitch response is left to the coupled wing/tail aerodynamics

effective_angle_limit_deg.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: fit of the runtime tanh bound to Roskam Part VI Fig. 8.13 K' at c_f/c 0.21 (FAST-GA digitization), tau 0.562

aerodynamic_gain.source: full shared flap law (no sensitivity variant)

stall_shift_fraction.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: 1 - dClmax/dCl0 of a plain flap, Roskam Part VI Figs. 8.31-8.33 (FAST-GA digitization) at t/c 0.149, c_f/c 0.21, mean over 15-45 deg; section lift slope 6.0/rad

lift_reference_offset_m.source: research/p51/p51-05/derive_physics.py: flap camber lift at the wing's 25 % MAC: its distance aft of the wing-body ARP, which the calibrated fuselage term moved forward
